biography.plain_text: Giovanni ‘Gianni’ Agnelli was an Italian industrialist who inherited interests in his family's Fiat business and led its international expansion. Born in Turin, he chaired the carmaker from 1966 to 1996, overseeing the addition of brands including Ferrari, Lancia and Alfa Romeo. He remained honorary chairman until his death in 2003.

long_biography.plain_text:
Gianni Agnelli and his wife Marella opened their art collection to the public through the Pinacoteca Agnelli in 2002. Their donated works are housed above the former Fiat factory at Lingotto, in a gallery designed by Renzo Piano. Agnelli had visited museums with his father as a boy, learning to see art as an education in taste.

Agnelli also established an independent research foundation, the Fondazione Agnelli, to mark his grandfather's centenary in 1966. He chaired the foundation for more than three decades. Its research addressed economic and social development, with particular attention to science, education and young people's prospects.
